chunks: And with this chain, Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said:

Rajab is a great month. Allah multiplies the good deeds in it and erases the bad deeds in it. Whoever fasts one day from Rajab, Hell will be distant from him by a journey of a hundred years. And whoever fasts three days, Paradise becomes obligatory for him.

key_terms.النَّارُ: Hellfire, the place of punishment in the afterlife.
key_terms.الْجَنَّةُ: Paradise, the eternal abode of bliss.
key_terms.رَجَبٌ: Rajab, the seventh month of the Islamic lunar calendar, known for its spiritual virtues.
key_terms.صَامَ: Fasted, referring to the act of observing sawm (fasting).
key_terms.يُضَاعِفُ: Multiplies, referring to the increase in reward for good deeds.

ai.seo_question: What are the rewards of fasting in the month of Rajab according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kadhim (peace be upon him) elucidates the spiritual potency of Rajab, emphasizing that divine mercy amplifies rewards and expiates sins during this sacred month. The hadith establishes a tangible link between specific fasting durations and eschatological outcomes, noting that a single day's fast creates a century's distance from Hellfire, while three days guarantee Paradise, reflecting the Shia tradition of valuing voluntary acts of worship for their transformative spiritual impact.
